id: 306-君士坦丁大帝與馬克森提烏斯的戰爭
theater: 羅馬城北臺伯河米爾維安橋

battle.name: 君士坦丁大帝與馬克森提烏斯的戰爭
battle.theater: 羅馬城北臺伯河米爾維安橋
battle.brief: 公元306年夏，君士坦丁在不列顛被軍隊推舉為帝，隨後與盤踞意大利的馬克森提烏斯對抗六年。312年10月28日，兩軍在羅馬城北臺伯河上的米爾維安橋隔河列陣，君士坦丁以「此標誌之下必勝」的旗幟破陣，馬克森提烏斯死於橋上追兵的擁擠與河水。卡面的科林斯青銅盔早在七個世紀前就已退入博物館，它留下的卻是重裝步兵靠隊形作戰的邏輯。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 這場戰爭是羅馬帝國內戰的一場，兩個交戰方在法理上都自稱羅馬人。戴克里先於293年設立的四帝制，把帝國分給四名奧古斯都與凱撒，規定帝位按功績傳承、不按血緣；君士坦丁一方走的正是這條路線。公元306年，戴克里先與馬克西米安相繼退位，君士坦丁之父君士坦提烏斯·克洛盧斯成為西部的奧古斯都，卻在同年2月病逝於不列顛的約克；7月25日，駐軍將領把二十多歲的君士坦丁推上皇帝的位置，這是歐洲西部軍隊推立君主的又一個先例，也是這場內戰的起點。君士坦丁能掌握的不列顛與高盧軍團，多半出自克洛盧斯與戴克里先時代的老兵系統；308年他在卡農圖姆迎娶馬克西米安之女福斯塔，與元老院認可的羅馬城政權短暫聯手，隨即在311年加利里烏斯頒布塞拉西亞敕令、否認馬克森提烏斯奧古斯都頭銜之後分道揚鑣。君士坦丁在西方的正統性來自兩件事：軍隊的效忠，以及他自稱的復仇——為父雪恨、討伐暴政；他同時握有鑄幣權與元老院式的文書程序，而這套程序在他取得羅馬之前一直拒絕承認他。對面的馬克森提烏斯是馬克西米安之子，306年由羅馬元老院與禁衛軍推舉為奧古斯都，掌控意大利、羅馬城與城市的稅收與糧食，並且獲得元老院多數與城市菁英的支持；他不是軍隊推立的產物，而是城市與議會推立的產物，這一點決定了他必須守住羅馬而不能退讓。加利里烏斯曾於306與307年兩度攻打意大利都未能根除他；308年馬克西米安一度復位，試圖讓兒子正式成為共治者，卻在同年被加利里烏斯處決於馬西利亞；311年塞拉西亞敕令承認馬克西米努斯·達亞與李錫尼烏斯為奧古斯都，馬克森提烏斯被削去頭銜，羅馬落入被圍攻的恐懼之中；312年他趁東方皇帝馬克西米努斯入侵意大利之機反攻，逼得對方部下叛變、馬克西米努斯死於塔爾蘇斯，意大利只剩他一人。此時君士坦丁的軍隊從高盧越過阿爾卑斯山向羅馬推進，兩軍在羅馬城北的米爾維安橋相遇，六年內戰在一天之內見了分曉。
countriesEn: This war was a civil war inside the Roman empire, and both sides claimed the Roman name in law. The tetrarchy that Diocletian had established in 293 deliberately made the imperial office a prize of merit rather than of blood, and Constantine's camp was the side that lived by that rule. When Diocletian and Maximian abdicated in 306, Constantius Chlorus, Constantine's father, became Augustus in the west, but died at Eboracum (York) in Britain in February of the same year; on 25 July the garrison acclaimed the young Constantine as emperor, one more precedent for the armies of the western provinces making emperors, and the opening move of this civil war. The troops Constantine could count on in Britain and Gaul were largely the old professional system of Constantius' and Diocletian's age. In 308 he married Fausta, daughter of Maximian, at Carnuntum, briefly allying himself with the Roman establishment that the Senate recognised; the alliance collapsed once Galerius issued the edict of Serdica in 311 and stripped Maxentius of the title of Augustus. Constantine's legitimacy in the west rested on two things: the loyalty of troops, and a self-appointed role as avenger of his father and destroyer of a tyrant. He also held the minting of coin and the paperwork of senatorial government, and that establishment had refused to acknowledge him until he took Rome. His opponent, Maxentius, was the son of Maximian and had been raised as Augustus by the Roman Senate and the praetorian guard in 306; he controlled Italy, the city of Rome, its taxes and its grain, and he held the support of most of the Senate and of the urban elite. He was not the product of an army acclamation but of the city and the assembly, and that fact decided that he had to hold Rome and could not give way. Galerius campaigned against him in Italy in 306 and 307 without rooting him out; Maximian returned to power in 308 in a last effort to regularise his son's position, and was put to death by Galerius at Massilia in the same year. The edict of Serdica in 311 recognised Maximinus Daia and Licinius as Augusti and condemned Maxentius as a usurper, and Rome sank into the fear of siege. In 312 Maxentius took the offensive while Maximinus was invading Italy, forcing that emperor's own troops to mutiny and leaving Maximinus dead at Tarsus in early 313. Italy then stood with Maxentius alone, and Constantine's army came down from Gaul across the Alps to meet him at the Milvian Bridge north of the city, where six years of civil war were settled in a single day.
people: 君士坦丁（Flavius Valerius Constantinus）約生於272年的尼什，是克洛盧斯與海倫娜之子，自幼隨父在宮廷與軍中生活，父皇在位時他已擔任軍職，並在302至303年對阿勒曼尼人的戰役中隨軍作戰。父親在約克病逝後，他立刻被士兵推舉，並在同年的克里維萊魯姆之戰中擊敗法蘭克人聯軍，鞏固了不列顛的基地。他的母親海倫娜在312年率領隊伍於維泰利亞追上兒子，帶來紫袍與金錢，歐瑟比烏斯把這段描寫成天命與母愛交會的場面；海倫娜此後成為帝國最受敬重的人物之一，數年後朝聖耶路撒冷。君士坦丁的長子克里斯普斯在311年已為執政官，後在313與317年擔任高盧與不列顛的指揮者，325年卻被父親處死，理由至今不明。馬克森提烏斯這邊同樣有被推上高位的人：他的禁衛軍與元老院是最初推舉他的力量，禁衛軍首領阿布拉比烏斯在309年奧斯蒂亞的敗仗中被打散；308年復位的馬克西米安是他的父親，卻在馬西利亞被加利里烏斯下令處決，成為整場衝突的轉折點。加利里烏斯是壓制馬克森提烏斯的主力，他311年在西爾米烏姆病逝，311年塞拉西亞敕令出自他手；戴克里先的外甥馬克西米努斯·達亞在311年接替東方的奧古斯都，312年率軍進入意大利卻被自己部隊拋下，313年初死於塔爾蘇斯，這一死讓意大利的對峙只剩君士坦丁與馬克森提烏斯兩家。記述這場戰爭的史料同樣有主角：歐瑟比烏斯是凱撒雷亞的教會領袖、君士坦丁的同時代人，他在《君士坦丁傳》裡記錄了軍隊推舉、暴風雨與米爾維安橋的細節，但明顯偏袒君主；拉克坦西烏斯是克里斯普斯的導師，在《迫害者之死》中記載了「此標誌之下必勝」的夢兆與盾上的十字，立場是基督教護教者；較晚的佐西莫斯則引述更早的記載，補充了橋上崩潰的細節。三人不約而同提到同一件事：馬克森提烏斯的名字在官方紀錄中被抹去，而君士坦丁進入羅馬時沒有像前輩那樣清洗城市。
peopleEn: Constantine (Flavius Valerius Constantinus) was born around 272 at Naissus, the son of Constantius and Helena, and grew up moving between court and camp; he already held a military command under his father and campaigned against the Alemanni in 302 and 303. When his father died at York, the soldiers acclaimed him at once, and in the same year he defeated a Frankish confederacy in the battle of Crivellerum, which secured his base in Britain. His mother Helena came up with a train and caught him up at Vitellia in 312, bringing the purple and money; Eusebius presents the scene as the meeting of providence and maternal devotion. Helena became one of the most respected figures of the empire and made a pilgrimage to Jerusalem a few years later. Constantine's eldest son Crispus was already consul in 311 and later commanded in Gaul and Britain in 313 and 317, but was put to death by his father in 325 for reasons that remain unclear. Maxentius's side had its own men raised by acclamation: his praetorian guard and the Senate were the forces that first acclaimed him, and the praetorian prefect Ablabius was broken by the defeat at Ostia in 309; his father Maximian, restored to power in 308, was executed by Galerius at Massilia, and that execution became the turning point of the whole conflict. Galerius was the man who had kept pressing Maxentius, and he died of illness at Sirmium in 311, the same year in which the edict of Serdica went out under his authority. Diocletian's nephew Maximinus Daia succeeded to the eastern Augustus in 311, entered Italy in 312 and was abandoned by his own troops, dying at Tarsus in early 313; that death left Italy with only two claimants, Constantine and Maxentius. The sources too have their protagonists. Eusebius of Caesarea, a church leader and contemporary of Constantine, recorded the acclamation, the storm and the details of the Milvian Bridge in his Life of Constantine, with a bias plainly in favour of the emperor. Lactantius, tutor to Crispus, wrote in De Mortibus Persecutorum of the dream and the sign and the cross painted on the shields, from the standpoint of a Christian apologist. The later Zosimus quotes earlier material and adds the detail of the bridge collapsing. All three make the same two points: that Maxentius's name was struck from the official record, and that Constantine entered Rome without the sack and the reprisals his predecessors would have given. A generation of civil war had, in effect, been decided in a single night at one bridge.
kits: 卡面是科林斯青銅盔，約公元前650年定型，希臘重裝步兵的制式頭盔：整副殼形覆住頭顱，只留兩條水平眼縫與一道鼻脊開孔，護頰可以上翻或放下。它在這場戰爭裡不是裝備，而是一件對照件：到公元306年，它退出軍隊已近八百年。但它確立了三項原則，正是米爾維安橋兩軍仍在服用的邏輯。第一，以正面厚度承受衝擊，不靠躲閃；第二，犧牲視野與聽覺換取防護；第三，戴它的人只能靠隊形活——希臘方陣之所以成立，正因為穿戴者看不清側後。到了四世紀初，羅馬重裝步兵頭上戴的是另一副東西：西部流行的帝國高盧式與城市間式頭盔，以及更接近決戰年代的脊冠盔，一九二八年在杜拉－歐羅波斯出土的一批鐵片與青銅配件即為其例，額前有脊線與護額，護頰以鉸鏈與皮帶固定，後頸加甲。它是科林斯盔那種閉合面甲構思的後裔，但改為可以單手迅速戴脫、比較透氣、壞了能換件的量產貨。防護的另一面是盾：半圓柱面的大盾從肩到膝，正面厚達數指，正是科林斯盔那個用正面吃住矛尖的想法的放大版。步兵的骨架是札甲：西部軍團仍用鐵片札甲，東方與蠻族出身的部隊多用鎖子甲，兩層疊穿的辦法在四世紀初已很普遍。兵器是短劍與加長的劍、重標槍與近身刺槍；投射火力方面，橋頭那一批弓箭手決定了戰局，而攻城用的球形弩與扭力弩在此役並未出現，因為雙方都沒有打攻城戰。真正走遍全軍的是那面旗幔：拉克坦西烏斯記載盾上繪著十字架、旗上帶有君士坦丁的頭像，這面後來叫作拉巴魯姆的旗幔是全軍的視覺中心。交通與補給方面，意大利的城鎮與羅馬城的糧食是這場戰爭的底氣，軍隊自不列顛與高盧經阿爾卑斯山口南下的路線決定了速度。
kitsEn: The card shows a Corinthian helmet, a type fixed around 650 BC as the standard headgear of the Greek heavy infantry: a shell enclosing the whole skull, with two horizontal eye slits and a slit at the nasal, and cheek pieces that could be raised or dropped. In this war the helmet is not equipment but a foil: by AD 306 it had been out of service for close to eight centuries. What it had established, however, were three principles that both armies at the Milvian Bridge were still living by. First, the blow is taken on the thickness of the front rather than dodged. Second, protection is bought at the price of vision and hearing. Third, the wearer can only survive by formation, which is exactly why the Greek phalanx worked, since the man inside the helmet could not see behind himself. By the early fourth century the headgear of Roman heavy infantry was something else: the Imperial Gallic and intercity types still current in the west, and, closer to the date of the battle, the ridge helmets, a group whose iron and bronze fittings were excavated at Dura-Europos in 1928, with a ridge and brow guard at the front, cheek pieces hinged and strapped, and a neck guard behind. They descend from the same closed-face idea as the Corinthian shell, but they were made to be put on or taken off with one hand, to breathe better, and to be replaced in parts when damaged. The other face of that protection was the shield: the semi-cylindrical scutum reaching from shoulder to knee, several fingers thick at the front, which is the Corinthian idea of taking the spear-point on the front enlarged to the size of a man. The infantryman's frame was mail and plate: the western legions still wore the segmented plate armour, eastern and barbarian units the mail shirt, and wearing one over the other was already common in the early fourth century. The weapons were the short sword and the longer spatha, the heavy pilum and the thrusting spear. On the fire side, the archers posted at the head of the bridge decided the battle, while the ballista and the onager never appeared in this action, since neither side fought a siege. What did travel through the whole army was the banner: Lactantius records crosses painted on the shields and the emperor's own portrait on the flag, and this standard, later called the labarum, was the visual centre of the army. On movement and supply, the towns of Italy and the grain of the city of Rome were the real wealth behind this war, and the rate at which the army came down from Britain and Gaul through the Alpine passes was decided by the route it took.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術主體集中在最後一天。君士坦丁從高盧出發後刻意輕裝急行，歐瑟比烏斯說他的軍隊只帶短程糧食、並禁止士卒劫掠，因此得以在敵人意料之外出現在米爾維安橋北面；兩軍隔河相望，馬克森提烏斯守住那座單孔石拱橋，把弓箭手擺在橋頭，兵縱隊沿弗拉米尼亞大道向羅馬延伸，陣地右翼壓在橋上，等於把整條退路握在自己手裡。君士坦丁沒有立刻強攻，他的營地設在米爾維安橋以北的山地，步兵展開成互相搭接的盾牆，騎兵收在兩翼，中央壓著那面帶十字的旗幔。首日交鋒後雙方拉鋸，歐瑟比烏斯記載君士坦丁曾把右翼推前、牽動敵陣，再收回重組，試圖在僵持中找出對方防線的縫隙。決定性的一刻是一場暴雨：雷雨驟至，天色昏暗，馬克森提烏斯陣中的弓箭手最先崩潰，離開了他們據守的橋頭；君士坦丁的騎兵就在雨中發動衝鋒，從中央直插敵軍縱深，密集的盾牆被衝開一道缺口，全軍隨即崩潰。追兵與敗兵一起湧上窄橋，橋在擁擠下被壓垮，橋上的步兵連同追兵一起墜入臺伯河；馬克森提烏斯本人在退路上溺斃。就戰術層面說，這場戰爭有兩點值得記住：其一，進攻方選擇了敵方地形最脆弱的一點——橋頭，那裡守軍最密卻最無處可退；其二，決定性的一擊交給了速度而不是重量，密集步兵在窄橋這種地形上反而是弱點。值得記取的失敗也在同一處：馬克森提烏斯把大批部隊壓進狹窄通道，把一場可能只是退卻的潰敗變成了全軍的滅亡。
tacticsEn: The tactics of this war are concentrated into its last day. Constantine moved out of Gaul with a deliberately light and fast column; Eusebius says his army carried only short-dated rations and that plunder was forbidden to the soldiers, which is how he appeared before the Milvian Bridge from the north against the enemy's expectation. The two armies faced each other across the river. Maxentius held the single-arched stone bridge, posted archers at its far end, ran his columns of infantry back along the Via Flaminia towards Rome, and rested his right wing on the bridge itself, which meant keeping the whole line of retreat in his own hands. Constantine did not attack at once. His camp was pitched on the heights north of the bridge, his infantry was deployed as a wall of interlocked shields, his cavalry was held back on the flanks, and in the centre stood the banner with the cross. The first day ended in a stalemate, and Eusebius records that Constantine pushed his right wing forward, pulled the enemy line, then withdrew and re-formed, trying to find a seam in a front that would not open. The decisive moment was a rainstorm: thunder and darkness came down, the archers in Maxentius's line were the first to break and abandoned the bridgehead they were holding, and Constantine's cavalry charged straight through the rain into the depth of the enemy line. The dense shield wall was opened in one place and the whole army came apart. The fugitives and the pursuers ran onto the narrow bridge together, the bridge was crushed by the weight of the crowd, and the infantry on it and the men chasing them went into the Tiber. Maxentius himself drowned on the line of retreat. Two tactical lessons follow. The attacker chose the most fragile point of the enemy's ground, the head of the bridge, where the defenders were thickest but had nowhere to go. And the decisive blow was given to speed rather than to weight, because dense infantry on a bridge was itself the weakness. The failure lies in the same place: by crowding his troops into a narrow causeway, Maxentius turned what might have been a retreat into the destruction of his entire army.
data: 先看能核對的數字。這場戰爭從公元306年7月25日君士坦丁在不列顛約克被軍隊推舉算起，到312年10月28日米爾維安橋決戰，前後六年三個月。歐瑟比烏斯《君士坦丁傳》記君士坦丁的步兵約兩萬、騎兵另計，這是本役最常被引用的雙方兵力數字；馬克森提烏斯一方的兵力沒有可靠記載，拉克坦西烏斯只說對方人數較多，後世估計從三萬到五萬不等，但無從核實，因此不取任何一個為準。地理數字比較可靠：米爾維安橋在羅馬城牆外約三英里，步行不到兩小時，是北方道路進入羅馬的門戶，橋為單孔石拱橋，寬度只容數列並行，正是這種寬度造成後來的踩踏與溺斃。溺斃者的數目在古代作家之間並不一致：歐瑟比烏斯說橋被擁擠的人群壓塌、無數人為河水所吞，拉克坦西烏斯也記下大批士兵溺斃，但具體數字無法核實，本篇只作定性記載。時間點倒是明確的：決戰日為10月28日；君士坦丁於10月29日進入羅馬城；元老院在12月將奧古斯都的頭銜與凱旋的榮譽授給他；313年1月他在羅馬城外另晉封為帕特里基烏斯；同年他與李錫尼烏斯會於米蘭，頒布宗教容忍敕令。錢幣也留下數字：勝後一批以SPES PVBLICAE（國家之望）為銘的銅幣與盾徽銀幣陸續發行；另一面，馬克森提烏斯的名字從此不見於官方銘刻與錢幣，而他那座未完成的巴西利卡諾瓦大巴西利卡由君士坦丁接手完成，是這場戰爭留下的最大一座羅馬建築。
dataEn: Start with the numbers that can be checked. From the acclamation of Constantine at York in Britain on 25 July 306 to the decision at the Milvian Bridge on 28 October 312, the war ran six years and three months. Eusebius' Life of Constantine gives Constantine's infantry as about twenty thousand, with the cavalry counted separately, and this is the most often quoted figure for the two sides; there is no reliable figure for Maxentius's army, Lactantius saying only that the enemy had more men, and later estimates ranging from thirty to fifty thousand without anything to support them, so none of them is adopted here. The geographical figures are sounder. The Milvian Bridge lay about three miles outside the walls of Rome, less than two hours' walk away, and it was the gateway through which the roads from the north entered the city; it was a single stone arch whose width allowed only a few columns abreast, and that width is what produced the crushing and the drowning afterwards. The number drowned differs between the ancient writers: Eusebius says the bridge gave way under the crowd and that a host were swallowed by the river, and Lactantius likewise records a great number of soldiers drowned, but the exact figures cannot be checked, so only the qualitative statement is kept here. The chronology, by contrast, is clear. The battle was fought on 28 October; Constantine entered the city on 29 October; the Senate conferred the title of Augustus and the honour of a triumph on him in December; in January 313, outside the city, he was additionally raised to the patrician rank; and in the same year he met Licinius at Milan and issued the edict of religious toleration. The coinage keeps a record too: after the victory a series of copper pieces and silver medallions with the legend SPES PVBLICAE, the hope of the state, was struck. On the other side of the ledger, the name of Maxentius disappears from the official inscriptions and from the coins, while the Basilica Nova he had begun and Constantine finished remains the largest Roman building the war produced.
cause: 打起來的緣由有四層。最底下一層是皇位繼承原則之爭：戴克里先的四帝制刻意規定帝位按功績而非血緣傳遞，馬克西米安卻在退位後仍圖讓兒子馬克森提烏斯取得奧古斯都位，306年由羅馬元老院與禁衛軍公開推舉，等於向元老院與城市傳統讓步，也等於挑戰四帝制的核心。於是加利里烏斯在306與307年先後用兵意大利，試圖把這條血緣線掐斷；308年馬克西米安一度復位並帶著君士坦丁的支持回到帝國，談判在卡農圖姆破裂，同年他在馬西利亞被處決，311年塞拉西亞敕令正式把馬克森提烏斯定性為僭主並剝奪其頭銜。第二層是君士坦丁個人的復仇旗幟：其父克洛盧斯306年病逝於約克，敵意宣傳把死因說成元老院下毒，這類說法出自較晚的史家；君士坦丁把自己打扮成替父雪冤、討伐暴政之人，藉此繞過元老院尚未承認他的尷尬。第三層是宗教：戴克里先303年發動的大迫害在此時尚未完全平息，加利里烏斯在311年才放棄迫害並頒下塞拉西亞敕令；君士坦丁在戰陣上高舉基督教符號，基督教社群與軍隊中的基督徒士兵因此成為他的助力，這層敘事在戰後被歐瑟比烏斯與拉克坦西烏斯反覆放大。最後是時機：311年加利里烏斯在西爾米烏姆病逝，312年東方皇帝馬克西米努斯·達亞入侵意大利時被自己部隊拋棄、313年初死於塔爾蘇斯，意大利的權力真空讓君士坦丁得以在不必兩面作戰的條件下東進；而羅馬城的穀物稅與意大利城市菁英的支持，是任何一個西部軍頭都覬覦的資源。
causeEn: There are four layers to the reasons for the war. The deepest is a conflict of principles over succession: the tetrarchy of Diocletian had deliberately ordered that the imperial office pass by merit and not by blood, yet Maximian, even after his abdication, still schemed to get the title of Augustus for his son Maxentius, who was acclaimed in 306 by the Roman Senate and the praetorian guard. That was a concession to the senatorial and urban tradition and at the same time a direct challenge to the core of the tetrarchy. Galerius accordingly campaigned against Italy in 306 and 307 to cut the hereditary line. In 308 Maximian returned to power with the support of Constantine, the talks at Carnuntum broke down, and he was executed at Massilia in the same year; the edict of Serdica in 311 then branded Maxentius a usurper and stripped him of his title. The second layer is the personal banner of revenge carried by Constantine: his father Constantius died of illness at York in 306, and hostile propaganda made the cause a poisoning by the Senate, a story found in later historians. Constantine dressed himself as the man who avenged his father and struck down the tyrant, and so sidestepped the awkward fact that the Senate did not yet acknowledge him. The third layer is religion. The great persecution launched by Diocletian in 303 had not yet fully ended, and it was Galerius who abandoned the persecution and issued the edict of Serdica in 311. Constantine carried Christian symbols into the battle, which made the Christian communities and the Christian soldiers in the army his supporters, and that narrative was amplified after the war by Eusebius and Lactantius alike. The last layer is timing. Galerius died at Sirmium in 311; in 312 the eastern emperor Maximinus Daia was abandoned by his own troops while invading Italy and died at Tarsus in early 313. The vacuum over Italy let Constantine advance east without having to fight on two fronts, and the grain tax of the city of Rome together with the support of the Italian urban elite was the resource that every soldier of fortune in the west coveted.
impact: 這場戰爭結束了四帝制的最後一段，也把羅馬皇位取得的方式永久改寫。此後一百多年裡，羅馬皇帝越來越多由軍隊推舉產生：君士坦丁的例子說明，軍隊的歡呼比元老院的決議更能決定皇位歸屬，這條路一直走到西羅馬帝國滅亡為止。帝國的權力結構也跟著變：君士坦丁在312年廢除禁衛軍，把它的番號與任務併入城防的都市大隊，改由跟隨皇帝的常備野戰軍與固定於邊疆的駐軍分擔，晚期帝國的兵役結構由此成形。宗教上的轉折更為徹底：313年的米蘭敕令恢復基督徒的自由，教會獲得財產與司法地位，基督教從受迫害的教派變成帝國的正式夥伴，直到君士坦丁本人在337年臨終受洗之前，政策的方向就已確定；十字與君士坦丁字母自此出現在旗幔、盾面、錢幣與建築上，315年的君士坦丁凱旋門成為這套圖像的紀念碑。對元老院而言，這是一場屈服：元老院不再是皇位來源，只能追認既成事實。馬克森提烏斯的記憶則被系統性抹除，馬克西米安的黨羽被清洗，羅馬城在劫掠與報復邊緣被君士坦丁按住，這份克制成為他統治的關鍵資產。反過來說，馬克西米安父子開的先例也不可回頭：出身於達爾馬提亞與希臘的軍人家庭先後登基，開啟了四世紀大量非羅馬出身者進入皇室的時代，最終分裂出拉丁西方與希臘東方的兩套帝國。
impactEn: This war closed the last act of the tetrarchy and permanently rewrote the way the Roman imperial office was acquired. For more than a century afterwards, Roman emperors were increasingly the creatures of army acclamation: Constantine's case showed that the acclamation of the troops decided the imperial office more effectively than any resolution of the Senate, and that road ran all the way to the end of the western empire. The structure of imperial power changed with it. In 312 Constantine abolished the praetorian guard, folding its name and its tasks into the urban cohorts of the city watch, and divided the work between the comitatenses, the field army that travelled with the emperor, and the limitanei, the garrisons fixed on the frontiers; the service structure of the late empire took shape here. The religious turn was more complete still. The edict of Milan in 313 restored the freedom of the Christians, gave the church property and standing in the courts, and turned Christianity from a persecuted sect into a recognised partner of the empire, and the direction of policy was fixed long before Constantine himself was baptised on his deathbed in 337. The cross and the Chi-Rho of Constantine appeared from then on on banners, on shields, on coins and on buildings, and the Arch of Constantine of 315 became the monument to that imagery. For the Senate the war was a submission: it was no longer a source of emperors but only a body that could give retrospective recognition to accomplished facts. The memory of Maxentius was systematically erased and the partisans of Maximian were purged, while Rome was held back from sack and reprisal at the brink; that restraint became one of Constantine's chief assets as a ruler. The precedent set by Maximian and his son, in turn, could not be undone: a soldier family from Dalmatia and Greece had reached the throne twice, opening the fourth century to the many non-Roman hands that would grasp it, and eventually splitting the empire into a Latin west and a Greek east.
result: 公元312年10月28日，馬克森提烏斯在米爾維安橋的追兵中被水淹死，羅馬城政權當夜崩潰，橋上的踩踏與河中的溺斃是本役最慘烈的一場。10月29日君士坦丁進城，軍令禁止劫掠，元老院以歡迎的行列迎接他，隨後授以奧古斯都與不可勝者的頭銜；馬克森提烏斯的遺體依禮葬於 Campus Martius，其子小馬克森提烏斯保留了執政官的名位，這是君士坦丁對敗者展示的第一份克制。然而同一時間，清算也開始：馬克西米安一系的支持者被逐一追究，馬克森提烏斯的名字從錢幣、銘文與官方年表中消失，禁衛軍被解散、番號改授都市大隊。到313年初，帝國西部只剩君士坦丁一人；313年他與李錫尼烏斯會於米蘭，頒下宗教容忍敕令，君士坦丁本人則在321年下了一道偏向基督徒的詔令，開了皇帝直接介入宗教的先例。戰場上的收穫很快變成制度：禁衛軍廢除、常備軍與邊軍分立、皇帝旗幟與軍團旗幟的差別化、與軍隊綁定的俸給與賞賜，晚期帝國的軍事骨架在此時已經成形。往後十四年，西部大致安寧，直到324年君士坦丁與李錫尼烏斯在克律索波利斯一戰中再決出獨裁，帝國才真正合為一人。若把這場戰爭看成一場技術性的勝利，它留下的規矩是：以窄地形的脆弱點作為主攻方向，把決定權交給速度與象徵，而把敵軍的退路當成戰場的一部分來經營。
resultEn: On 28 October 312 Maxentius was drowned among the crowds on the Milvian Bridge, the government of the city of Rome collapsed that night, and the crushing on the bridge and the drowning in the river were the worst slaughter of the action. On 29 October Constantine entered the city under an order against plunder, was received by the Senate in procession, and was then given the title of Augustus and of unconquered one. Maxentius's body was buried with the full honours in the Campus Martius, and his son, the younger Maxentius, was allowed to keep the dignity of consul, the first piece of restraint Constantine displayed towards a defeated enemy. At the same time the reckoning began: the partisans of the Maximian house were pursued one by one, the name of Maxentius vanished from the coins, the inscriptions and the official fasti, and the praetorian guard was disbanded, its name passing to the urban cohorts. By the beginning of 313 the west of the empire belonged to Constantine alone. In that year he met Licinius at Milan and issued the edict of toleration, and in 321 Constantine himself promulgated a ruling favouring the Christians, the first time an emperor had legislated directly on religion. What the battlefield gave was quickly turned into institutions: the abolition of the praetorian guard, the division of the field army from the frontier troops, the distinction between the emperor's own standard and that of the legions, and the tying of pay and bounty to the army, all of which formed the military skeleton of the late empire. The west then enjoyed some fourteen years of quiet until the war between Constantine and Licinius decided the sole rule at Chrysopolis in 324 and the empire was truly made one. Taken as a technical victory, this battle left a set of rules behind: strike at the fragile point of narrow ground, give the decision to speed and to a shared emblem, and treat the enemy's line of retreat as part of the battlefield to be managed.
